% 12.03.2025 CRL.M.A. 7927/2025(seeking permission to travel abroad)
1. Through this application, Petitioner seeks permission to travel to Australia for a period of 60 days to meet his son and grandson.
2. Issue notice.
Mr. Ripu Daman Bhardwaj, SPP, accepts notice on behalf of Respondent.
3. Counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant submits that he wishes to travel to Australia to meet his son due to some family issues faced by the Appellant's son.
The Appellant has provided the details of the address where he will be residing with his son in Australia.
It is further pointed out that previously by orders dated 13th August, 2019 and 28th April, 2023, Appellant was allowed to travel to Australia and Canada to visit his son and daughter.
This is a digitally signed order.

The Appellant did not misuse the liberty granted to him and complied with all the conditions imposed by the Court.

sentences.text:
4. Mr. Ripu Daman Bhardwaj, SPP, opposes the application and submits that the Appellant has been convicted for offences under Sections 120B/420/471 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 read with Sections 13(2)/13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which are serious in nature and in case he is permitted to leave India, he will misuse the liberty and not return.
5.
The Court has considered the afore-noted.
6. The sentence of the present Appellant was suspended vide order dated 09th October, 2018.

Since this Court has previously allowed the Appellant to travel abroad on two occasions and no incident has been reported that the Appellant has misused the liberty granted to him, the Court is inclined to entertain the Appellant's request.

7. Accordingly, the present application is allowed and the Appellant is permitted to travel to Australia for a period of 60 days from the date of his departure, on the following conditions:
(i) The date of departure should be within a period of 30 days from the date of passing of this order, i.e., 12th March, 2025, on Appellant furnishing a personal bond in the sum of INR 1,00,000/- with one surety, which should be a family member, of like amount to the satisfaction of the Registrar General of this Court.
(ii) Upon his arrival in Australia, the Appellant shall report to the Indian Embassy situated there and shall intimate the same to the Investigating Officer via e-mail.
(iii) The Appellant shall also provide contact numbers where he shall be This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 12/03/2025 at 22:27:22 available during his stay abroad and at least one of the said contact numbers shall be kept operational at all times, subject to all fair exceptions, including the period he is on board the aircraft.

He shall intimate to the Investigating Officer of any change in his mobile number.
8.
With the above directions, the application is disposed of.
SANJEEV NARULA, J MARCH 12, 2025 d.negi
